tier1.text: The small cardiac vein drains blood from the back surfaces of the heart's right side. This vein runs beside the right coronary artery, a vessel that supplies blood to the heart. The small cardiac vein lies in the coronary sulcus, a deep, fat-filled groove on the heart's surface. The small cardiac vein empties into the coronary sinus, a large vein on the back of the heart.

quotes.quote: A vein running parallel to the right coronary artery in the coronary sulcus that drains into the right extremity of the coronary sinus.

Also prominent is a series of fat-filled grooves, each of which is known as a sulcus (plural = sulci), along the superior surfaces of the heart. Major coronary blood vessels are located in these sulci. The deep coronary sulcus is located between the atria and ventricles.
